take_homes: The agent reviewing its own work is too kind. I need an independent reader, a fresh agent or me, and I should treat its report as a claim to check.
A rules file I keep sharpening carries what I learned into the next session, so I'm not re-explaining each time. I want one for the pricing work that the team shares.
Where the output is generic, my context was thin. I should add a specific detail rather than polish the prompt.

monday.move: Start a rules file from the pilot-cohort brief. Run a fresh cold-reader agent on it and ask where it sounds generic. Then fill the gaps with real numbers.
monday.who: Me, then one person from my team to test whether they can pick it up
monday.stop_condition: Stop when the cold reader's generic flags are down to things I can't fix without new data.
monday.blocker: The team has no shared place for the files. I'd start with a single copy in one folder and argue about tooling later.

misconception.why: Packaging the lesson into a file the next session reads felt more valuable than any single prompt, and the cold-reader trick was a method, not a phrasing. I still half think prompt skill matters most. The module never says in so many words that prompts are the wrong thing to focus on.

one_line: The rules-file and cold-reader ideas are useful, but I had to wade through the same corporate paragraph about a dozen times and the exercise was a personal website, not real work.
